preconditions.description: The number of glades n is between 1 and 10^6 inclusive.
The number of trails m is between 0 and 10^6 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n for x, y in trails)
preconditions.description: Each trail connects two glades with valid indices between 1 and n.
The list of trails contains exactly m entries.

postconditions.description: The output is a single non-negative integer string.

postconditions.expression: int(output_str.strip()) == max(0, (odd_degree_count // 2) + (1 if not connected_component_has_trails and m > 0 else 0) + (1 if m == 0 else 0) - (1 if m > 0 and connected_component_has_trails and odd_degree_count == 0 else 0))
postconditions.description: The output integer represents the minimum number of trails to add: if m=0, 1 trail is needed (to form a loop on glade 1); if m>0, it is the number of odd-degree vertices divided by 2, plus 1 if the component containing glade 1 has no trails (requiring connection), otherwise just the odd-degree pairs. Note: This expression assumes 'odd_degree_count' is the count of vertices with odd degree in the component containing glade 1, and 'connected_component_has_trails' is true if that component has at least one trail.

postconditions.expression: int(output_str.strip()) == (0 if (m > 0 and all(d % 2 == 0 for d in degrees_in_component_1) and len(trails_in_component_1) == m) else (len([d for d in degrees_in_component_1 if d % 2 != 0]) // 2 + (1 if len(trails_in_component_1) == 0 else 0)))
postconditions.description: Refined logic: If all vertices in the component containing glade 1 have even degrees and all trails are in this component, output 0. Otherwise, output (count of odd-degree vertices in component 1) // 2, plus 1 if the component containing glade 1 has no trails (meaning glade 1 is isolated from the existing trails).
